title: Flexible Returnship, Sabbatical, and Hybrid Work Policy
author: Alexandra Chen
body:
Overview:

This page describes Redwood's combined policy for flexible work arrangements, the formal Returnship program (for employees re-entering the workforce), and our Sabbatical offering for tenured contributors. The goal is to make career re-entry, sustained caregiver support, and long-form refresh cycles predictable, fair, and low-friction — while keeping team-level planning and customer commitments intact.

Key principles:
- Equitable access: programs apply consistently across departments where operationally feasible.
- Predictability: clear timelines, approval steps, and impact on compensation/benefits.
- Manager partnership: managers work with people-ops on role coverage and ramp plans.
- Business continuity: funding, backfills, and knowledge transfer plans are required for all multi-week changes.

Who this applies to:
- Full-time Redwood employees (exempt and non-exempt) and long-term contractors with 12+ months tenure where noted.
- Candidates returning to Redwood after a voluntary separation within 5 years (see Returnship eligibility).

1) Flexible Work (Hybrid and Part-Time Options)

Short summary:
Redwood supports hybrid work by default. Employees may request reduced-hours or formalized part-time arrangements on a case-by-case basis. The standard expectation for most IC and manager roles is 32–40 hours/week pro rata unless role requires different coverage (e.g., 24/7 support, sales East/West coverage).

Eligibility and common configurations:
- Hybrid (default): up to 3 remote days/week with office days agreed by team.
- Remote-first: for roles approved by the manager+people-ops; requires clear timezone and overlap agreements.
- Reduced hours / Part-time: 60%–80% FTE common; below 60% requires VP approval and benefits changes.

Decision factors (manager checklist):
1. Does the role require synchronous coverage (customer support, oncall)?
2. Is the candidate/employee timezone compatible with core team hours?
3. What measurable deliverables and SLA changes are required?
4. Is there a backfill or reallocation plan?

Approval and documentation:
1. Employee submits Flexible Work Request form (People-ops Google Form link in Related Pages).
2. Manager drafts a 4-week transition and coverage plan, including measurable success criteria for the first 90 days.
3. People-ops reviews for policy compliance and benefits impact; HR notifies payroll and benefits teams.
4. Formal agreement documented and stored in HRIS (work arrangement, start date, review cadence).

Review cadence: 30/90/180 days or sooner on request.

2) Returnship Program (Re-entry Path for Experienced Hires)

Program intent:
Returnship helps professionals who took a multi-year career break (typically for caregiving, health, education, or other personal reasons) return to impactful roles at Redwood with structured ramping, mentorship, and a clear pathway to permanent offers.

Eligibility:
- Prior full-time employment (not required to be at Redwood) and a minimum 1–3 year career break within the last 5 years.
- Candidates may be external hires (open cohort) or Redwood alumni returning within 5 years of separation.
- Must meet core role qualifications (interview bar) with interview process tailored to account for employment gaps.

Program structure (example cohort model):
- Duration: 12–16 weeks paid placement (contractor or fixed-term employment depending on role and location).
- Time allocation: typical 30–40 hours/week with flexible scheduling.
- Mentor pairing: each returnee is paired with a senior peer and a people-ops sponsor.
- Curriculum: targeted onboarding, project-based deliverable(s), weekly coaching, and monthly evaluation checkpoints.

Outcomes and conversions:
- Successful completion evaluated by manager + mentor against a defined checklist (technical proficiency or product impact, collaboration, independent contribution).
- Typical conversion: 60–80% convert to regular full-time employment within 4–8 weeks post-placement; conversion terms negotiated and documented.

Budget and hiring:
- Hiring manager budgets 75% of a full-role recruitment cost into the hiring plan for a returnship placement.
- People-ops maintains a small central fund to support training and cohort-specific tooling.

3) Sabbatical Policy (Extended Time-Off for Tenured Contributors)

Purpose:
Sabbaticals are intended as a paid or partially paid multi-week leave to support rest, professional development, or caregiving beyond standard parental leave. They are an earned benefit to encourage retention and long-term growth.

Eligibility and tiers:
| Tenure (continuous service) | Sabbatical length | Pay while on sabbatical | Benefit continuation |
|---------------------------:|:------------------:|:-----------------------:|:-------------------:|
| 3–4 years                 | 4 weeks            | 50% base pay            | Health benefits maintained for up to 12 weeks |
| 5–7 years                 | 6–8 weeks          | 75% base pay            | Health benefits maintained for sabbatical period |
| 8+ years                  | 12 weeks           | 100% base pay           | Health benefits maintained and incidental stipend (up to $2,000) |

Process to apply:
1. Employee submits a Sabbatical Request to their manager with proposed dates at least 90 days in advance.
2. Manager and employee co-create a handoff and coverage plan (including a prioritized 8-week backlog and oncall delegation if required).
3. People-ops confirms eligibility, pay continuation, and records dates in HRIS.
4. For sabbaticals >8 weeks, VP approval is required.

Re-entry expectations:
- Employees must complete a 2-week reboarding plan (reduced deliverable expectations) and a 30-day check-in with manager + people-ops.
- Extended absences may trigger a light performance calibration to set expectations on ramp.

4) Interaction with Parental Leave, Medical Leave, and Benefits

- Sabbatical is separate from statutory parental or medical leave and may be taken before or after those leaves (subject to local law and payroll rules).
- Benefit eligibility (401k/retirement matching, equity vesting schedule, paid time accrual) during reduced hours, returnships, or sabbaticals will follow the standard HRIS rules; people-ops will provide a benefits impact summary at approval time.

5) Manager and Team Responsibilities

Managers must:
- Draft a coverage plan and a 90-day success plan for the returning or transitioning employee.
- Coordinate hiring/backfill budgets with finance if temporary headcount is required.
- Assign a primary peer mentor for returnship participants and confirm weekly touchpoints.
- Put in-place lightweight knowledge transfer (KT) docs, runbooks, and a recorded 30/60/90 handoff session.

6) Example Scenarios (quick reference)
- Scenario A: Software engineer returns after 18 months for caregiving. Manager requests a 16-week Returnship placement at 30 hours/week, mentor assigned, conversion evaluated at week 12.
- Scenario B: Product manager requests a 6-week sabbatical after 6 years of service for professional development; manager approves, sets coverage, and schedules 30-day reboarding.

7) FAQ
Q: Does sabbatical count as employment tenure?
A: Yes, sabbatical counts as continuous service for tenure-based benefits and equity vesting unless local law states otherwise. People-ops will confirm specifics per jurisdiction.

Q: Can a returnship be remote?
A: Yes, returnships may be remote if the role and timezone constraints allow. Onsite onboarding week is recommended but not mandatory.

Q: How do part-time arrangements affect equity vesting?
A: Equity vesting continues pro rata based on the new FTE percentage unless otherwise negotiated at approval.

8) Metrics and Program Health (people-ops tracking)
- Time-to-coverage for roles with reduced-hours: target < 6 weeks for common IC roles.
- Returnship conversion rate: target 65%+ annual conversion to full roles.
- Sabbatical retention delta: measure 12-month retention post-sabbatical vs matched cohort.
